heading: Terminology
text: Terminology

heading: Terminology
text: **Module instance:** One Runtime-known realization of a module owned by exactly one Runtime. It has one Runtime-scoped instance identity, one Runtime-owned lifecycle, and optional persistent-state, placement, presentation, and provider state. The owning Runtime controls its Logos lifecycle semantics. A module instance identity MAY remain stable across stop/start cycles when the Runtime host or deployment preserves that identity.

heading: Terminology
text: **Consumer:** The module instance whose authority is used for an operation. Runtime authenticates the consumer at the invocation boundary. A route is established for exactly one consumer, and only that module instance may use it. Consumer is a relationship in an operation or route rather than a separately managed entity. A module-instance address identifies the consumer. The address does not authenticate the module instance or grant authority. Runtime MUST preserve the addressed module-instance identity while it is needed to keep active routes and retained authority or audit material unambiguous.

heading: Terminology
text: If a later specification needs a human, user-session, device, organization, or agent identity, it must define that identity and its delegation relationship explicitly.

heading: Terminology
text: When a module performs an operation, Runtime binds that module instance as the consumer and active authority policy must permit the consumer and requested operation.

heading: Terminology
text: Changing execution mode MUST NOT silently change the module interface contract observed by callers.

heading: Terminology
text: Every system service provider MUST be a local module provider backed by a local module instance.

heading: Terminology
text: Runtime MUST maintain ordinary provider and lifecycle records for their module instances.

heading: Terminology
text: A system service provider MAY use direct mode or local transport mode according to active policy and the applicable profile.

heading: Terminology

heading: Terminology
text: Remote facades and external host or deployment services MUST NOT be bound as system service providers in this revision.

heading: 8.1 Module Initialization Inputs

text: 9. Runtime-Control Interface

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST accept a Runtime Control invocation only from an authenticated module instance.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST authorize the consumer and requested method, target, and observation scope according to active policy before executing an operation, except that `report_failure` uses the caller-bound authorization rule in Section 9.3.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: A runtime instance MUST have an authority policy for runtime-control operations, route establishment, system service access, provider visibility, lifecycle control, and remote-runtime enrollment.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Before Runtime binds an initial system service provider, Runtime MUST have bootstrap authority policy established by its runtime host or deployment inputs.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Bootstrap policy MAY identify initial system service providers and grant only the operations needed to validate and reach those providers.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: A candidate provider MUST NOT select, bind, or authorize itself as an authority-bearing system service.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST authorize each initial system service binding from bootstrap policy rather than from the candidate provider or another provider that is not yet bound.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime startup MUST establish the initial orchestration realization under bootstrap policy.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: When Module Loader is used, its initial provider MUST be established first and used to realize orchestration.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: When authority policy is externalized, bootstrap policy MUST identify the orchestration instance and the operations and targets it may use to establish the selected initial Capability Authority.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Orchestration MUST establish that binding before starting the remaining deployment under active authority policy.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Before using a local-transport system service provider, Runtime MUST complete the authorized Transport Hello exchange for the required module contract.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST NOT use the provider for dependent operations until all binding checks succeed.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: If an external Capability Authority is unavailable, Runtime MUST deny operations that depend on it unless bootstrap policy defines a narrower recovery path.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: If no authority policy allows an operation, the runtime MUST deny the operation.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: For authority-policy evaluation, Runtime MUST authenticate the consumer at the enforcement boundary and use the consumer identity defined by LOGOS-MODULE-CAPABILITY-AUTHORITY.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MAY derive policy attributes from authenticated context.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST populate or validate the Capability Authority request's `consumer` against the authenticated consumer for the attempted operation.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST reject a returned decision whose consumer does not match the request.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: When authority policy denies an operation, the runtime MUST NOT perform the operation and MUST report an authorization failure through the method, transport, or runtime API error channel used for the attempted operation.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST fail closed for the attempted operation, but it MUST NOT record an authority-evaluation failure as an explicit policy denial unless policy returned a deny result.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: The caller-facing error may remain an authorization failure, but retained observation or audit material MUST distinguish denial from evaluation failure.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: System-service operational errors MUST NOT be treated as authority decisions or denial reasons.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: The runtime MUST retain enough authority-decision material to explain allow/deny enforcement through Runtime Control observation or implementation audit logs.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: That material SHOULD include the consumer reference, the attempted operation, the target provider or route when present, and the decision identifier when present.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: Runtime MUST compute every request and successful-response payload commitment at the Runtime-controlled invocation boundary, independently of whether authority policy requires audit retention.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: It MUST bind each root to the selected route, provider, contract, method declaration, and exact request or response type for that call.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: When the decision requires retention, Runtime MUST produce the `call` audit record defined by LOGOS-MODULE-CAPABILITY-AUTHORITY.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: It MUST derive each retained request or response commitment from the schema-typed value at the enforcement boundary, not from an unverified root or contract identifier supplied by the provider or consumer.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: If a remote runtime is not enrolled or otherwise accepted by authority policy, the local runtime MUST NOT use it for remote-module facades or remote routes.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: When a target Runtime accepts an operation forwarded by an enrolled source Runtime, the source Runtime MUST identify the module instance that it authenticated locally as the consumer.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: The target Runtime MUST verify that the consumer reference's `runtime_instance_id` matches the authenticated source Runtime identity and that active policy permits that Runtime to forward operations for consumers it owns.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: For a remote Runtime Control connection, the source Runtime MUST place the exact Logos deterministic-CBOR encoding of that consumer's `logos.runtime.module_instance_address` in the first Transport Hello `token` field.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: The target Runtime MUST decode that single value, apply the ownership and forwarding checks above, and bind every Runtime Control invocation on the connection to that consumer.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: The source Runtime MUST use the connection only for that consumer and close it when it no longer authenticates that module instance as the consumer.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: A missing, empty, malformed, non-deterministic, trailing-byte, or ownership-mismatched value MUST produce Transport ProtocolError `NOT_AUTHORISED`, establish no session, and execute no Runtime Control method.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: The token is a consumer reference protected by source-Runtime authentication; it is not a route ticket or grant of authority, and the Hello response token MUST be empty.

heading: 9. Runtime-Control Interface
text: It MUST NOT be represented using a fabricated consumer reference.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Runtime MUST authenticate and authorize every Runtime Control invocation independently for its consumer before applying a state mutation.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Concurrent invocations from the same or different consumers MUST NOT share consumer identity, authority decisions, or request-key scope.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Runtime MUST apply mutations that affect the same module instance, route, listener, or provider export in one total order.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: That order MUST respect completion order when one invocation completes before another begins.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Each mutation MUST observe the complete result of earlier mutations in that order and MUST change its target atomically.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Operations on independent targets MAY proceed concurrently.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: For a request carrying `expected_execution_revision`, the target MUST resolve to a local module instance.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Runtime MUST compare that revision atomically with lifecycle acceptance and reject a mismatch without mutation, including for otherwise idempotent requests.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Concurrent lifecycle requests MUST NOT create duplicate realizations, native contexts, destruction calls, or release operations.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: A `start_module` request for an instance in `loaded` or `ready` MUST return its current module state without creating another realization or replacing retained intent or its origin.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: A `stop_module` request for an instance in `stopping` or `unloaded` MUST return its current module state and MUST NOT initiate another destruction or release.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: An explicit stop MUST cancel retained execution intent, including when the instance is already `stopping` or `unloaded`.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: If `stop_module` is ordered after an incomplete start or recovery, Runtime MUST prevent that attempt from later making the instance `ready`.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: If `start_module` is ordered while the instance is `stopping`, it MUST fail and MUST NOT schedule an implicit restart.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Once `close_route`, failure, or revocation places a route in a terminal state, a later renewal MUST fail and MUST NOT revive it.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: An observation concurrent with a mutation MAY report the complete state before or after that mutation.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: It MUST NOT combine fields from different versions of the same record.

heading: 9.1 Concurrent Runtime Control Operations
text: Runtime MUST emit lifecycle and route-state events for one target in the same order as the corresponding committed state transitions.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Runtime MUST authorize this method independently for the target instance.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: The target MUST belong to the Runtime exposing the invoked contract; Runtime MUST reject a target owned by another Runtime without forwarding the query or substituting a facade.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: `selection` MUST report the retained accepted implementation selection when one exists and MUST otherwise be omitted.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: `selection.package` MUST be present exactly when that selection retains a selected package identity; its `package` and `version` carry the identity strings defined by LOGOS-PACKAGE-MANIFEST.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Runtime MUST NOT infer this identity from installed inventory, a version requirement, or a newer available package.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Other realization mechanisms MUST use `implementation-specific`; transport mode alone does not establish a concrete placement.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Runtime MUST report `unknown` when realization ownership or its correspondence to the selection cannot be confirmed, including an unresolved realization attempt or cleanup outcome.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Retained selection MUST NOT be reported as a current realization merely because it survived a stop, failure, or Runtime restart.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: The response MUST NOT include artifact paths, configuration values, credentials, or invocation descriptors.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Runtime MUST reject the request unless intent is `requested`, the instance is `unloaded` or `error`, and cleanup of any previous realization is complete.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Recovery MUST preserve the intent, its origin and any retained package selection, and MUST recheck current execution authority, trust, prerequisites and realization acceptance.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Loss of the initiating consumer's connection or execution MUST NOT by itself cancel retained intent or prevent recovery.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Runtime MUST retain the authenticated origin and the provenance needed for current trust and execution authority checks across connection loss and Runtime restart.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Retained provenance MUST NOT authenticate a new invocation by that consumer.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Runtime MUST authenticate the report through the Runtime Control binding supplied for that realization and verify that the binding still belongs to the current realization.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: A remote Runtime binding or another module's binding MUST NOT authorize reporting failure of that realization.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Authorization for this method consists of these checks and MUST NOT depend on a policy grant or availability of a Capability Authority provider.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Runtime MUST reject a report that lacks the required realization-bound association with `NOT_AUTHORISED`.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Runtime MUST reject a report whose associated realization is no longer current or whose module state is neither `loaded` nor `ready` with `NOT_READY`, without changing lifecycle state or execution intent.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: On acceptance, Runtime MUST handle the report as a realization failure under Section 10.1, preserving execution intent and its origin.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: A report accepted during initialization MUST prevent that realization from becoming `ready`.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Failure handling MUST allow the reporting invocation to return without waiting for cleanup.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Cleanup MUST preserve the applicable invocation-quiescence and native-context lifetime requirements.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: A report MUST NOT initiate recovery or affect a replacement realization.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Runtime MUST select one accepted declaration for `module` under active policy or fail the request.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Runtime MUST atomically create the record with a fresh instance identity, lifecycle state `unloaded`, and execution intent `uninitialized`.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Runtime MUST retain a successful key-to-instance association while the created instance remains known.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: A repeated request with that key and the same `module` MUST return the same instance without changing its lifecycle or execution intent.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Reusing the key with a different `module` MUST fail as an invalid request.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Concurrent requests with the same key MUST NOT create multiple instances.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: If the module record is not known, Runtime MUST report an invocation failure through the shared error channel defined by LOGOS-MODULE-INTERFACE.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: The failure MUST preserve this section's non-disclosure rules.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: A request rejected by invocation authorization, target selection or the lifecycle checks in Section 9.1 MUST NOT change execution intent or its origin.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: For a local instance in `unloaded` or `error`, acceptance MUST establish `requested` intent with the authenticated requesting module as its origin before execution authorization or startup.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: A subsequent startup denial or failure MUST NOT cancel that intent or change its origin.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: For an instance in `loaded` or `ready`, the request MUST preserve existing intent and origin as required by Section 9.1.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: If no ambiguity exists, the caller MAY omit `instance`.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Runtime MUST authorize it as a Runtime-wide operation; authority to stop individual modules does not authorize shutdown.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: On acceptance, the engine MUST close admission to new lifecycle operations, routes and instance-dependent calls.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Accepted requests MUST share one engine-owned shutdown sequence under Section 10.2, independent of caller cancellation.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: The engine MUST attempt the response before tearing down its invocation path; response loss MUST NOT cancel shutdown.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: If the runtime cannot determine fresh remote state, it MUST report uncertainty through `state` and `reason` rather than reporting the provider as `ready`.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Runtime MUST deliver Runtime Control state events only while the authenticated subscriber remains authorized to observe the referenced module, provider, or route.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: A Runtime Control subscription MUST NOT reveal unrelated provider inventory, route state, event publishers, or subscribers.

heading: 9.3 Runtime-Control Module Contract
text: Implementations MAY use different internal structures, but call evidence MUST be derived from the CDDL-defined runtime-control value.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: Failure of a local module realization MUST NOT by itself terminate Runtime or trigger shutdown of independent module realizations.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: Runtime MUST report the failure and continue startup and operation of independent modules.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: An unavailable prerequisite MUST prevent dependent startup or operations that require it, without by itself terminating an otherwise healthy dependent realization.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: The orchestration module MUST evaluate the active restart policy and schedule permitted recovery through `recover_module`.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: The Runtime host or deployment MAY supply that policy as protected input.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: Enabled policy MUST bound retry frequency and MAY limit attempts; retry accounting MUST survive orchestration restart and lost responses.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: An explicit stop or Runtime shutdown MUST cancel pending automatic recovery.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: A ready module that detects an unrecoverable internal failure preventing it from fulfilling a declared role MUST invoke `report_failure` through its owning Runtime Control binding.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: An ordinary invocation failure MUST NOT by itself be treated as a report of realization failure.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: The Runtime engine MUST detect realization failure, mark the instance as `error`, fail its routes, and arrange cleanup through the mechanism that established the realization.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: It MUST use the same mechanism for accepted recovery.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: The engine MUST enforce current execution authority and resource bounds independently of orchestration.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: The realization mechanism MUST NOT independently decide whether a failed module is restarted.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: Accepted recovery uses a new realization, including a new native context where applicable, and MUST complete the full lifecycle before readiness.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: A stop caused by permission withdrawal MUST preserve execution intent.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: When required permissions become available, orchestration MUST request resumption of that intent through `recover_module`, including deployment intent initially blocked by missing permissions.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: The engine MUST continue enforcement and operation of independent modules and MUST NOT autonomously restart orchestration.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: Another authorized module MAY restore orchestration, or protected construction may establish it when the Runtime host restarts.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: A successful recovery MUST NOT reactivate routes that failed with the previous realization.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: Runtime MUST complete the ordinary system-service binding and readiness checks before using a restarted system service provider.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: The failed provider MUST NOT be invoked to restart itself.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: While a required system service is unavailable, Runtime MUST fail every operation that requires it.

heading: 10.1 Module Failure and Restart
text: That unavailability alone MUST NOT change the lifecycle state of an otherwise healthy module realization unless continued execution would exceed current authority.

heading: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown
text: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown

heading: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown
text: The Runtime engine MUST apply the following procedure to accepted `shutdown_runtime` requests and host-initiated graceful shutdown, independently of orchestration availability.

heading: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown
text: Shutdown MUST preserve retained execution intent and its origin.

heading: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown
text: If an ordinary realization does not complete cleanup within the active grace period, Runtime MAY request forced cleanup through the responsible realization, Runtime host, or deployment mechanism. Forced termination of the execution envelope MAY prevent destruction from beginning or returning.

heading: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown
text: If a locally realized module fails during startup before it reaches `ready`, Runtime MUST use the same realization mechanism to release and clean up the partially realized implementation.

heading: 10.2 Graceful Shutdown
text: Runtime MUST NOT leave a failed startup realization available as an unregistered or ready module provider.

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: 13.2 Host Lifecycle

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: Successful startup MUST establish the initial system-service bindings required by Section 9.

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: The Runtime MUST manage its own execution progress after startup without requiring the host to run a particular event loop or periodically call the Host Embedding API.

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: An accepted shutdown request MUST continue independently of the requesting or waiting thread.

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: Repeated shutdown requests MUST refer to the same shutdown procedure.

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: Waiting for shutdown MUST NOT itself initiate shutdown.

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: A host MAY wait on a separate thread while another thread requests shutdown.

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: Shutdown initiated through Runtime Control MUST be observable through the same wait operation.

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: The host MUST serialize construction, binding registration, startup, and destruction for a given Runtime instance.

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: Destruction MUST NOT overlap another Host Embedding API call on that instance.

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: The Runtime MUST reject destruction while execution or cleanup can still use the handle or its retained resources.

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: A rejected destruction attempt MUST leave the handle valid.

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: The host MUST retain registered native code and borrowed binding resources until successful destruction.

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: A Runtime that has not started MAY be destroyed directly.

heading: 13.2 Host Lifecycle
text: A startup or shutdown failure MUST NOT implicitly destroy the handle.

13.3 C Interface
text: The implementation MUST document each supported identifier and its configuration semantics, including how protected bootstrap and deployment inputs are supplied.

heading: 13.3 C Interface
text: An unsupported identifier or invalid configuration MUST be rejected with `LOGOS_ERR_INVALID_PARAMS`.

heading: 13.3 C Interface
text: `configuration` contains exactly `configuration_len` bytes in that format and MAY be null only when the length is zero.

heading: 13.3 C Interface
text: The host MUST supply a function with the signature required by LOGOS-MODULE-INTERFACE for that symbol.

heading: 13.3 C Interface

heading: 13.3 C Interface

heading: 13.3 C Interface
text: Runtime MUST make the registered binding available to the applicable process-local ABI caller.

heading: 13.3 C Interface
text: Registration alone MUST NOT create a module instance, initialize a module, or grant authority.

heading: 13.3 C Interface
text: Duplicate binding identifiers, duplicate symbol names, empty symbol tables, or null symbol addresses MUST be rejected with `LOGOS_ERR_INVALID_PARAMS` without changing an existing registration.

heading: 13.3 C Interface
text: Runtime MUST copy any data it retains after those calls return.

heading: 13.3 C Interface

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: Required pointers MUST be non-null, strings MUST be NUL-terminated UTF-8, and supplied memory MUST remain valid for the call.

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: Null required pointers MUST be rejected with `LOGOS_ERR_INVALID_PARAMS`.

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: The host MUST supply live Runtime handles returned by this implementation; arbitrary forged or stale pointers need not be detected safely.

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: For a valid `out_runtime` pointer, construction MUST set `*out_runtime` to null before processing other inputs.

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: A failed registration MUST NOT retain any part of the supplied binding.

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: Startup may be attempted only once per handle and MUST NOT begin after shutdown has been requested.

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: Invalid registration or startup ordering MUST return `LOGOS_ERR_NOT_READY`.

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: If shutdown is requested through Runtime Control during bootstrap, startup MUST return `LOGOS_ERR_CANCELLED` unless it has already completed.

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: Repeated waits MUST report the same completed result.

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: Destruction is permitted only before the first startup attempt or after shutdown completion, and MUST return `LOGOS_ERR_NOT_READY` while execution or cleanup still requires retained resources.

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: Only shutdown-request and shutdown-wait calls may overlap on the same handle; the host MUST serialize all other calls against every Host Embedding API call on that handle.

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: The host MUST NOT wait for shutdown from a Runtime callback or module invocation whose completion shutdown may require.

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: Their storage MUST be isolated from calls on other threads and remain valid until the next Host Embedding API call into the same implementation on the calling thread or unloading of that implementation, whichever occurs first.

heading: 13.4 Results And Call Ordering
text: Other failures MUST use the applicable shared error code, or `LOGOS_ERR_MODULE` when no more specific shared code applies.
